ai.description: *Cnemaspis indica* is a small gecko reaching 40 mm snout-vent length. It is brownish-grey with a distinct dark vertebral stripe and yellow-spotted flanks. It features keeled scales and round pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Cnemaspis indica* is the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, keeled tubercles forming lateral rows along its flanks.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis indica* inhabits the high-altitude shola forests and rocky outcrops of the Nilgiri Hills in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nilgiri Dwarf Gecko is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects across rock surfaces and tree trunks during the sunlit hours of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis indica* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis indica* is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests and grasslands of the Nilgiri Hills in the Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu and Kerala, India.
